Notes: Buy cells from a battery dealer, not a marketplace: fakes with inflated capacity are common. Store ships in the US for about $5.

Must-match spec: Must be the M38 (M18 and M28 have no amp). About 45 x 20 mm; the pocket is 45.6 x 20.6 mm
Notes: Pick the variant "M38 MICRO". The CAD is modelled on the DFRobot DFR0720, which is the same MH-M38 module.

Must-match spec: USB-C, about 28 x 17 mm, three chips on the board: TP4056 + DW01A + 8205A
Notes: Pick the variant "5PCS 18650 type-c". A board with only one chip has no battery protection; do not use it with this cell.

Must-match spec: Round, 40 mm diameter, 20 mm tall or less, 4 ohm
Notes: The seller's drawing shows 40 x 19 mm. Anything taller than 20 mm hits the cell. The second driver is a spare.

Must-match spec: Pure nickel, 0.15 mm thick, 8 mm wide
Notes: Pick the variant "0.15mm". Nickel-plated steel is cheaper but takes solder badly. Spot-weld the tabs to the cell.

Must-match spec: M2, 8 mm long, self-tapping, head no wider than 4.2 mm
Notes: Pick the variant "8mm/50pcs M2". The lid recesses are 4.4 mm across; if the heads are wider, use any M2 x 8 pan-head self-tapper instead.

Must-match spec: SPDT, body about 8.6 x 3.6 x 3.5 mm, 4 mm lever
Notes: Pick the variant "Handle length 4mm". It sits in the recess on the inside of the end wall with the lever through the slot.
Base and lid are 56 cm3 of plastic if printed solid, so a normal print uses less.
